subject: Post-call: Luminex latency sensitivity + concurrency probe
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference>
To: Mallory Stevens <mallory@luminexsys.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 15:08:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: Luminex latency sensitivity + concurrency probe

Thanks again for the time today, Mallory — good discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on the SLO probe scope.

Key asks from Luminex (as I captured them)
- Target envelope: p95 end-to-end < 200ms for single-turn generation (avg prompt ~350 tokens); p99 < 600ms.
- Streaming: WebSocket streaming for token-by-token UI; acceptable first-byte (TTFB) for stream start < 50ms.
- Concurrency: steady-state concurrency target 8–12 concurrent streams per region; occasional burst to 40 for 30s windows.
- Throughput: baseline 30 req/s (1–2 tokens/sec profile), peak 150 req/s for short spikes.
- Model constraints: currently using a Llama2-derived 13B; willing to evaluate Redwood hosted variants (fp16 vs int8 quantized).

Open items for Luminex to confirm
1) Traffic envelope JSON (QPS distribution + token length histogram) — you mentioned SRE can share traces.
2) Whether all traffic will originate from a single NA region or multi-region failover.
3) Any hard SLA windows (business-critical hours).

Redwood proposal for the probe
- Run a two-day sensitivity sweep: Day 1 = p95-focused latency runs at 8, 16, 32 concurrency; Day 2 = p99/backfill runs simulating KV-cache misses, longer prompts, and burst spikes.
- We will test both hosted API (default runtime with prefix/KV caching enabled) and a dedicated-reserved pool config to show delta vs your incumbent.
- Deliverables: traffic-shaping harness results, p95/p99 tables, per-route token breakdown, and a short recommendations doc.

Attachments: I attached a working "slo-sensitivity-matrix" and a sample traffic envelope schema for your SRE.

Next steps
- Mallory / SRE: share traffic envelope + sample traces by EOD Friday (2026-12-04).
- Redwood: propose test window and test endpoints by tomorrow (12/03).
- Agreement: confirm that the probe can hit your staging API keys and that streaming endpoints are reachable from our test runner.

Thanks — I pasted a condensed action list below. Happy to jump on a 15m to lock the window.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.inference | +1 (415) 555-0114

Attachment stubs: slo-sensitivity-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet), luminex-traffic-envelope.json (json)

From: Mallory Stevens <mallory@luminexsys.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference>
Cc: sre-team@luminexsys.com, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 18:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: Luminex latency sensitivity + concurrency probe

Thanks, Jonas — solid recap. A few clarifications from our side: 
- p95/p99 targets: those numbers reflect our UI SLAs. We can tolerate p95 up to 220ms for some heavy prompts (500–700 tokens), but p99 needs to stay < 700ms during business hours.
- Streaming: we use an incremental chunking protocol over WebSocket; typical TTFB expectation is < 70ms in NA, can be looser for EU.
- Concurrency: 10 steady streams is safe; burst to 45 for ~20–45s is realistic once per 6–8 hours.
- Traffic: attaching a sanitized 24h trace (sample) and a histogram of prompt sizes. SRE will follow up with a pcap-like summary if needed.

We can provide staging keys and open firewall to Redwood test runners (IP range listed below) for a 48h window.

SRE contact: sre-team@luminexsys.com (they have the traces and egress constraints).

Mallory
Mallory Stevens
Head of Platform, Luminex Systems
mallory@luminexsys.com

--- Forwarded attachment list ---
- luminex_24h_trace_sanitized.json (sample traces)
- prompt_size_histogram.csv (summary)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference>
To: Mallory Stevens <mallory@luminexsys.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>, sre-team@luminexsys.com
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: Luminex latency sensitivity + concurrency probe

Perfect — thanks for the artifacts, Mallory. We reviewed the prompt-size histogram and sample traces overnight. Proposed test plan (short):

1) Test window: 2026-12-10 06:00–18:00 PT (we request a 12-hour window to run repeated sweeps; we'll only use ~6–8h of active load).
2) Runner connectivity: Redwood will originate tests from the following CIDR blocks: 35.201.0.0/16, 34.120.0.0/16 (please confirm SRE allows these).
3) Test matrix highlights:
   - Hosted API baseline: prefix/KV caching ON, streaming enabled, standard fp16 runtime. Sweeps at concurrencies = [8,16,32,45 burst].
   - Dedicated pool variant: reserved capacity with relaxed batching and heat-up for KV cache priming.
   - A/B comparison: p95/p99 delta, first-byte times for stream start, and token-level cost estimates.
4) Edge-case probes: cold KV misses, 700+ token prompts, and controlled packet-delay injection for 250–500ms to emulate WAN tails.

We will upload the harness and raw results to the Drive folder I linked; summary will be a short 2–3 page deliverable plus optics in a spreadsheet.

Action for Luminex: confirm the CIDR allowlist and the 12/10 test window. If that works, we will post a formal test-run schedule and invite for a live monitoring call.

Attaching a short sensitivity matrix so you can see our planned concurrency sweeps.

—Jonas

Attachment stubs: 20261202-slo-sensitivity-matrix.xlsx

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: Luminex latency sensitivity + concurrency probe

Confirming we should enable the dedicated pool variant for the p99-focused runs. Karthik — please make sure quantized variants (int8) and prefix caching heuristics are available for the dedicated runs.

Small recommendation: start with a low batch target for streaming (1–4) to preserve tail latency, then gradually increase batch size for the throughput sweeps.

Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Product — Redwood Console

(On internal note: treat the burst window as a separate gating condition in the report; this is where incumbent often degrades.)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference>
To: Mallory Stevens <mallory@luminexsys.com>
Cc: sre-team@luminexsys.com, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 4 Dec 2026 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: Luminex latency sensitivity + concurrency probe

Mallory — quick follow to lock this in: can you confirm (A) CIDR allowlist and (B) approval for 2026-12-10 06:00–18:00 PT as the Redwood test window? Once SRE confirms, we'll upload the harness and schedule a 30m pre-run sync for instrumentation (traces, sampling).

Deliverables recap:
- p95/p99 per-run CSVs and visual plots;
- streaming first-byte (TTFB) and per-token pacing distributions;
- per-route cost delta (hosted vs dedicated) with ops recommendations (batching, cache TTLs, quantization).

HubSpot link for the deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DEAL-LX-7834

Thanks — looking forward to your confirmation.

—Jonas
